questions.q: Describe the achievements of the Kushanas under Kanishka.
answer: The Kushanas ruled a vast territory stretching from Central Asia into north India, and reached their height under Kanishka in the first and second centuries CE.

answer.text: Kanishka supported Buddhism, is associated with a Buddhist council, and under his rule Buddhism spread along the Silk Route into Central Asia and China.

Two great schools of sculpture flourished — the Gandhara school, which showed Greek influence, and the Mathura school, which was indigenous. Both produced some of the earliest images of the Buddha in human form.
The Kushanas controlled key trade routes and issued fine gold coins, making their empire prosperous and cosmopolitan.

questions.q: What do we know about the Sangam Age of the Tamil south?
answer: The far south during this period is known as the Sangam Age, after its remarkable literature.

answer.text: Tamilakam was ruled by three dynasties — the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas, together called the muvendar or three crowned kings.

Our main source is Sangam literature, early Tamil poetry composed in assemblies (sangams) traditionally held at Madurai, the Pandya capital. It vividly describes kings, warfare, love, trade and daily life.

The region carried on a brisk trade with the Roman world, exporting pepper and spices; Roman coins found in the south and the account in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea confirm this flourishing commerce.
